messages:
hana: Follow-up to the rollout metadata thread — I want to propose a small extension to the stamp model to support signed stamps and an explicit "attestation" field so runtime and ops can verify intent before doing optimistic rollforwards. Keeping it tiny but wanted to capture compatibility and migration risks.

pete: sounds interesting. paste the minimal example and explain how clients should behave when attestation is missing/invalid.

hana: example below. Key goals: (1) let control-plane optionally sign a stamp (signature + signer id) so runtime can make stronger safety choices; (2) keep client logic simple: ordered candidates + stamp_epoch check; (3) add an attest_status hint (ok/warn/invalid) for fast path.

```json
{
  "artifact_id": "auth-encoder-3b",
  "stamp": "v2026-06-01",
  "stamp_epoch": 11,
  "candidates": [
    {"type":"hash","id":"sha256:ab12","variant":"fp16","priority":0},
    {"type":"stamp","id":"v2026-05-28","variant":"int8","priority":1}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": "ordered",
  "attestation": {"signer":"release-bot","signature":"sig:...","issued_at":"2026-06-01T12:00:00Z"},
  "attest_status": "ok",
  "soft_expiry": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z",
  "preferred_seq_len": 1024,
  "stamp_origin": "auto-migrate"
}
```

hana: Notes: `attestation` is optional. `attest_status` is a short enum clients/runtime can use: `ok` => safe to rollforward aggressively in canary windows; `warn` => prefer prior candidate unless operator approves; `invalid` => treat as untrusted and avoid optimistic rollforwards.

samir: Two practical questions: (A) where do we validate signatures? control-plane or runtime? (B) how do we avoid fragmentation if older clients don't understand `attestation` or `attest_status`?

pete: for (A) prefer validating signatures in the control-plane at ingest and emitting `attest_status` as a derived field. runtime can optionally re-verify if runtime has keys, but it's not required. That keeps runtime cheap. For (B) default behavior for older clients: ignore unknown fields and use stamp_epoch + candidates order. So `attest_status` should be advisory only for backward compat.

samir: agree. Also recommend a short migration rule: when control-plane starts emitting `attestation`, also emit `stamp_epoch` bump and a telemetry flag `attest_migration=true` so we can monitor client adoption before changing routing behavior.

hana: good idea. i'll add `attest_migration` telemetry hint and a recommended rollout: start with `attest_status: warn` then move to `ok` once metrics look good.

attest-bot: schema-check: staging validator flagged unknown nested `attestation` structure; filed INF-8112. Suggest adding attest schema to central validator and a compatibility flag.

pete: operationally we should add an alert when a stamp's `fingerprint` changes while `attest_status` == `ok`. That likely indicates a bad publish. Don't auto-block but page ops.

samir: tenant override note: Dedicated tenants can request `enforce_attestation=true` per tenant profile, in which case control-plane must reject stamps without valid attestation for that tenant. Document precedence: tenant_override (highest) -> attestation enforcement -> default policy.

hana: action items:
- hana: update appendix with `attestation` schema, `attest_status` enum, and sample migration plan (ETA EOD).
- pete: add control-plane ingest validation for signatures and an alert rule for fingerprint+attest anomalies (ETA 2 days).
- samir: add telemetry flag `attest_migration` and monitoring dashboard to track client adoption (ETA 3 days).
- attest-bot: once schema updated, re-run validator.

pete: one more nit: make sure `attestation.signature` is small (e.g., base64 short token or reference to KMS-signed envelope) not full cert chains in payload. We'll store large material out-of-band if needed.

hana: agree; note in appendix that signature should be a compact token or reference and include signer id.

samir: sounds reasonable. if no objections i'll be fine merging the appendix after hana's edits. :+1:

attest-bot: INF-8112 tracked. Will re-run schema tests on merge.

hana: thanks all. short and practical.
